newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fresh slaughter in Algeria, 42 dead, say newspapers.
newsitem.headline: Fresh slaughter in Algeria, 42 dead, say newspapers.

text.p: Moslem rebels hacked to death 42 people in a village south of Algiers, the second massacre in Algeria within 24 hours, Algerian newspapers said on Thursday.
The victims, in Omaria village, Medea district, included 17 women and three babies, savaged by killers wielding axes and swords early on Wednesday, said El Watan newspaper.

There was no immediate official confirmation but El Watan is normally well-informed on security issues. Algerian authorities have in the past remained silent on similar killings which have subsequently been independently confirmed.
The slaughter brought to more than 300 the number of people killed in recent weeks and coincides with Algeria's countdown to its first parliamentary elections in more than five years.

Attackers moved into Omaria village only 24 hours after 93 people had their throats cut or were hacked to death with farm tools overnight Monday-Tuesday in the worst massacre in more than five years of violence.
Another newspaper, Liberte, said the 42 in Omaria, about 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, were killed by having their throats cut. Another 25 villagers were wounded, it said.
"This hamlet has already suffered one attack by armed groups during (the Moslem holy month) Ramadan in 1996 when 25 peaceful, defenceless villagers were assassinated," Liberte added.

News of the latest killing broke as condemnation grew over the earlier slaughter of the 93 people, including 43 women and girls. They died in an isolated farming community Haouch Boughlef-Khemisti, only 25 km (15 miles) south of Algiers.

"It's hard to remember a more vicious terrorist insurgency than this one, a more cynical group than these Islamic terrorists and they deserve special criticism and condemnation by the world community for these despicable acts," U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
The Algerian news agency APS said the Vatican had condemned the "terrifying massacre" which the Algerian government itself said was carried out with "unprecedented savagery".
"France is worried and shocked by the blind and savage nature of the violence hitting Algeria," its foreign ministry spokesman said.
Attacks on villages, particularly in the strongly Moslem fundamentalist area south of Algiers, started late last year.
The conflict erupted when authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election the now-outlawed Islamic Salvation Front was set to win. About 60,000 people have been killed.
Some village attacks are seen as attempts to destabilise the country, others to punish those who refuse to help rebels, or as revenge on relatives of rival groups or security forces.

Algerian political parties on Wednesday and Thursday condemned the Haouch Boughlef-Khemisti attack. The former ruling National Liberation Front said: "This barbarity is condemned by all religions, laws and morals of humanity."

El Watan said only around 20 people escaped unscathed out of the whole population of 150 in Haouch Boughlef-Khemisti. Some of the 25 villagers wounded in the attack remain in hospital in El Harrach suburb in Algiers.
One woman, in intensive care, with her throat cut, was able to whisper: "Using their knives, the terrorists opened up my stomach, as well as slashing my arm and leg."
A 15-year-old girl also lay there, her throat gashed. She could not speak.
